exact_advances: For p=6m+5 the parent 0/1/2 valuation blocks are exactly the Taylor-order blocks of b_{m,k}(epsilon)=(-5m-4+5epsilon/6)_k(-4m-3+2epsilon/3)_k/((k!)^2 2^k) at epsilon=0, evaluated at epsilon=p.
T01 is termwise divisible by p, while T02 and T11 are termwise divisible by p^2; only T00 requires genuine aggregate cancellation.
With B=4m+3, C=binom(2m+1,m), P_m(x)=2F1(-m,-m;m+2;x), the unit tail factors modulo p as T00 = 3*2^(-2B)*C^2*P_m(2)*(5P_m(2)+8P_m'(2)).
A_m=C*P_m(2)=sum_{k=0}^m 2^(m-k) binom(m,k) binom(2m+1,k) and A_m is congruent modulo p to 2^m P_{2m+1}(sqrt(2)/2)/(sqrt(2)/2).
Zhi-Hong Sun Theorem 4.5 gives P_{2m+1}(sqrt(2)/2)=0 mod p for p congruent 17 or 23 mod24, hence p divides A_m, P_m(2), G_p, and T00 for both requested classes.
Therefore every surviving finite-Clausen tail block is now proved to have at least one p factor in the minus classes, and the original mod-p^3 target is exactly normalized to one mod-p^2 certificate.

The normalized certificate is expanded into two finite scalar conditions R0 and R1 using explicit low/middle/high Taylor coefficients; these remain unproved all-prime and are the smallest residual unit of this execution.

imported_theorem.source: Zhi-Hong Sun, Congruences involving binom(2k,k)^2 binom(3k,k) m^{-k}, arXiv:1104.2789v3, Theorem 4.5
imported_theorem.statement_used: For primes p congruent 17 or 23 mod24, P_floor(p/3)(sqrt(2)/2) is congruent to 0 modulo p.
imported_theorem.scope_check: Here p=6m+5, so floor(p/3)=2m+1; also p is congruent 1 or 7 mod8, so sqrt(2) exists modulo p.

normalized_certificate.deformation_form: With G_p=F0+pF1+p^2F2 and H_p=J0+pJ1, set g0=F0/p+F1, g1=F2, tau0=T000/p+T001+U010, tau1=T002+U011+U020+U110. Then R0: g0*J0-tau0=-1 mod p; R1: (g0*J0-tau0+1)/p + g0*J1+g1*J0-tau1=0 mod p.

smallest_unresolved_identity: Prove R0 and R1 uniformly for p congruent 17 or 23 mod24, equivalently obtain the p^2 lift of the CM/reverse-tail factorization together with the first p-adic digits of the middle/high deformation blocks.
